exact_authored_statement_excerpt:
statement: >-
  Each authored area of the canonical tree — `docs/`, `docs/purpose/`, `docs/architecture/`,
  `docs/architecture/decisions/`, `docs/archive/` — MUST contain an `index.adoc`.
  Other canonical filenames are defined when useful and are NOT instantiated merely to satisfy an
  empty taxonomy (spec 2 §4).

statement: >-
  A documentation artifact declared at RATIFY MUST name a `path` that begins `docs/` and ends
  `.adoc`; an artifact with `action: archive` MUST name a `path` beneath `docs/archive/`. Core stores
  these paths as opaque strings and never interprets them (companion §3); interpreting them is this
  extension's job, because only the extension knows the tree.

statement: >-
  A file authored beneath `docs/` MUST be AsciiDoc (`.adoc`). An authored `.md` beneath `docs/`,
  outside the generated `docs/dist/` tree, is a violation. This is the format half of the
  documentation model handoff spec 2 §4 names; it is an EXTENSION obligation because core is
  forbidden to know what a `.adoc` is (companion §4, *Deliberately excluded*).

statement: >-
  No two authored documents beneath `docs/` may declare the same `:doc-id:`. Uniqueness is what makes
  `doc-id` an identity rather than a label, and it is the precondition for resolving any relationship
  edge to exactly one target (spec 2 §5.1).

statement: >-
  Every relationship attribute on an authored document (`:decides:`, `:supersedes:`, `:implements:`,
  `:depends-on:`) MUST name a `doc-id` that some document in the corpus actually declares. A target
  outside that set is a REPORTED finding. It is NEVER synthesized into a node, and never silently
  dropped. This is the one hard requirement of spec 2 §5.4 and the flagship rule of this extension.

statement: >-
  An authored `.adoc` beneath `docs/` MUST declare both a `:doc-id:` and a `:status:` attribute with
  non-empty values. `doc-id` is the document's node identity in the relationship graph (spec 2 §5.1);
  `status` is what makes the current-versus-historical boundary readable at all.

statement: >-
  When a repository documents itself (`docs/` exists) and its plan declares journeys or flow routers,
  `docs/purpose/journeys/` MUST contain exactly what `atdd-bun docs journeys` generates from `plan/`:
  `index.adoc` and one SVG per journey map, per journey's nominal path, and per routed user/system flow. A missing,
  stale, hand-edited, or extra file is a violation.

statement: >-
  The corpus MUST render with asciidoctor, and every internal cross-reference MUST resolve. A build
  failure or an unresolvable internal reference is a FAIL. An ABSENT toolchain, or a build failure
  the capability cannot attribute to a specific document, is `COULD_NOT_CHECK` — never `PASS`, and
  never `FAIL` (spec 2 §3, *What the capability owes core*, and §7).

statement: >-
  Any path in the change set beneath `docs/`, outside `docs/dist/`, MUST be covered by an artifact in
  the documentation declaration. An undeclared documentation change is a violation. This rule lives in
  the extension and NOT in core, because it requires knowing `docs/` (spec 2 §4; companion §4,
  *Deliberately excluded*).

statement: 'Feature names are seeded from product capability produce/consume artifacts: identify the artifact, determine
  its type, pick a type-specific verb, choose an object from the artifact''s domain/resource, and combine
  as {verb}-{object}.'
statement: Each feature is registered under exactly one product capability's _features.yaml manifest.

statement: A feature is the smallest independently-verifiable slice of a product capability's behavior
  — a bounded capability that declares a URN, a status, and a non-empty acceptance
  section, links to exactly one product capability, closes a feedback loop, and stays within its
  size limits. This node is an advisory semantic anchor — it enforces nothing directly;
  the enforceable parts of this meaning are decomposed into the constraint/rule nodes
  that require it.
statement: Estimate the architectural footprint from DESIRED OUTCOMES, interfaces, and component layers.

statement: 'A feature marked kind: feedback-loop must declare at least one SMOKE acceptance with a close_the_loop
  block containing consumer_reacted and drift_resolved.'

statement: 'An optional feature `kind:` classifies the system archetype; kind: feedback-loop marks a producer->consumer
  correction loop (detect+emit, receive+react, predicate no longer fires).'

statement: 'A docs-only feedback-loop feature may suppress the close-the-loop rule inline on the kind:
  line.'

statement: Architectural footprint = sum(component.count x weight[component.type]), rounded UP, mapped
  to a size bracket.

statement: Group DESIRED OUTCOMES into a feature by shared step, dimension, object, or coherent user story (<=10
  per group); avoid miscellaneous buckets.

statement: A feature must not exceed 2 new tables, 2 async jobs, or 2 integrations; exceeding any hard
  limit MUST trigger a split.

statement: A feature slug (the 3rd segment of feature:<capability>:<name>) must be verb-object
  — kebab-case, at least two tokens, the leading token a verb from the convention verb
  lexicon, and no connective tokens. Brand or proper-noun slugs must be listed explicitly
  in feature.convention.yaml verb_object_enforcement.brand_exceptions; an implicit
  exception is a violation.
statement: Feature YAMLs declare a urn, a status, and a non-empty acceptance section.

statement: Final feature size = max(desired-outcome-count size, Footprint size); features MUST be S or smaller, else
  split or stage before execution.

statement: A feature URN is feature:{capability}:{feature}, both kebab-case, the feature in verb-object form;
  built via URNBuilder.feature.

statement: A feature's size must equal max(DESIRED OUTCOME size, Footprint size); features exceeding component/event/hard
  limits must be split.

statement: The artifact type (event, state, data, config) determines the appropriate
  verbs for the feature name.

statement: A flow router is the domain-decomposition artifact for a diverging journey
  — it declares WHICH user/system flow is selected next when a journey branches, keyed by a produced
  artifact (the divergence signal), composing multiple strictly-linear user/system flows into a
  branching journey-of-journeys. It is a declared routing registry (artifact_urn ->
  user_system_flow_id), not an imperative map. This names the routing DECISION; the runtime that
  resolves and executes it (the route-control runner and its dispatcher) is a coder/tester
  concern. This node is an advisory semantic anchor — it enforces nothing directly;
  the enforceable parts of this meaning are decomposed into t

statement: Every entry in plan/_user_system_flows/_flow_routers.yaml must agree with the document
  it points at on every field it mirrors — theme, status and surfaces. The document
  is authoritative; the registry is discovery metadata, so a disagreement is always
  the registry being wrong.

statement: Every acceptance embedded in a DESIRED OUTCOME is an object whose `identity.urn` starts with `acc:`. Package rule,
  strict.

statement: Every participant and lifeline a flow router lists is either an external actor (`user:…`, `system:…`)
  or a typed reference to an artifact the plan declares. Package rule, strict.

statement: Every plan artifact whose kind the planner recognizes carries its canonical identity (`user_system_flow_id`, `flow_router_id`,
  `journey_id`, or `urn`). Package rule, strict.

statement: No two plan artifacts declare the same identity (`user_system_flow_id`, `flow_router_id`, `journey_id`, `urn`,
  …). Package rule, strict.
statement: Every `.yaml`, `.yml` or `.json` file under `plan/` parses. Package rule, strict.

statement: Every typed reference an artifact makes (`capability:`, `feature:`, `desiredOutcome:`, `user-system-flow:`, `flowRouter:`, `journey:`)
  names an artifact the plan declares. `contract:` references are resolved by the contract registry rules instead.
  Package rule, strict.

statement: Every recognized plan artifact (product capability, feature, DESIRED OUTCOME and its acceptances, user/system flow, user/system flow flow router,
  journey topology, registries) satisfies its JSON Schema in `planner-schemas/`. A violation that belongs to a canonical
  rule is reported under that rule (for example `planner.user-system-flow.naming`); every other violation is reported here.
  Package rule, strict.
statement: Every product capability a user/system flow lists under `capabilities:` is declared as `capability:<slug>`. Package rule, strict.

statement: Artifact names map to REST API endpoints of the form /{domain}s/{id}/{resource}[/{category}],
  with the resource term selecting the HTTP verb (POST/GET/PUT/DELETE) and category
  facets adding path segments.

statement: Produce/consume artifacts (WHAT) seed feature names (HOW) by combining
  a verb with the domain or resource - {verb}-{domain} when the domain is the focus,
  {verb}-{resource} when the resource is the focus - with verb choice driven by the
  artifact type (event, state, data, or config).

statement: Product capability artifacts carry a stable URN of the form contract:{domain}:{resource}[.{category}]
  that links the artifact to its contract independently of contract version, and the
  graph maintains bidirectional linkage between product capability URNs and contract IDs.

statement: Produce and consume artifacts are named domain:activity-verb for signals/events
  and domain:data-noun for state/data, where events are past-tense verbs, state is
  nouns/adjectives, and collections are plural.

statement: A product capability artifact URN that has no matching contract in the registry is a
  violation (an orphaned URN).

statement: The product capability that declares an artifact in produce[] is its producer and generates
  the artifact contract; a product capability that declares the same artifact in consume[] is a
  consumer and references the existing contract. An optional contract field on each
  entry points to the contract path.

statement: An artifact's contract directory layout follows one of three structures
  - FLAT, FACETED, or COLLECTION - determined by whether the name has a dot facet
  and whether the resource holds multiple schema files.

statement: Every leaf directory under contracts/ or telemetry/ (one containing .schema.json
  or signal .json files) must contain a tests/ subdirectory.

statement: 'Every #N entry in an issue body''s Dependencies section must carry a classification
  tag: prereq, merged, sibling, or parallel.'

statement: Every parent issue body must carry a populated Graph Context section, neither
  missing nor left as the injection placeholder.

statement: >-
  Starting from a journey's entrypoint flow router, every reachable flow router route must have a
  unique route_id and be accounted for exactly once by either a continuation or a terminal. A continuation's source route
  must exist, its declared artifact must occur in the linear user/system flow selected by that route, and its
  destination flow router must exist. Continuation or terminal declarations whose source flow router
  is unreachable from the journey entrypoint are invalid. Continuation cycles are rejected until an
  explicit loop construct defines bounded/intentional repetition.

statement: >-
  A journey is the declarative topology that composes routing decisions across flow routers.
  Flow routers remain local decision boundaries: each selects exactly one linear user/system flow. An exposed
  journey declares the journey router actions that start it and its first flow router. The journey
  owns what happens AFTER that selected user/system flow completes: a route may terminate explicitly, or a named
  artifact produced by the selected user/system flow may continue control at another flow router. A journey
  therefore composes flow router -> user/system flow -> flow router without making flow routers recursive and
  without moving product capability execution out of

statement: >-
    Journey strategies are candidate ways to meet declared behavioral obligations. Choose for latency, throughput, cost, reliability, determinism, and complexity requirements; none is universally best. This convention does not authorize bypassing flow routers, user/system flows, continuations, or acceptances.

statement: >-
  A plan that declares flow routers must declare at least one journey, and every flow router must be
  reached by a journey: either as a journey's entrypoint flow router or as the destination of a
  continuation reachable from that entrypoint. A flow router no journey reaches is a routing decision
  with no stated trigger and no stated place in the product flow.

statement: >-
    Choose among already declared valid strategies using workload or resource signals while preserving accepted outputs and route obligations.

statement: >-
    Combine compatible calls or computations to amortize I/O, setup, serialization or scheduling overhead without changing accepted logical results.

statement: >-
    Reuse valid results or recompute only affected portions when freshness and invalidation contracts make reuse safe.

statement: >-
    Run independent journey branches in parallel only when the topology explicitly specifies fan-out, dependency release, join, and failure semantics.

statement: >-
    Use a flow router's deterministic guards and priorities to select among declared linear user/system flow variants. A shortcut is a declared route, not an undeclared bypass.

statement: >-
    Overlap producers and consumers through incremental artifact delivery only with an explicit streaming protocol.

statement: >-
    Follow declared flow router routes and user/system flow continuations without additional scheduling or speculative transformations. Reference is the default, not a mandated slow path.

statement: >-
    Initiate reversible likely-needed work early only when discarded work and cancellation cannot change accepted behavior.

statement: 'Nothing is authored before the operator confirms the locked decomposition.
  The Ratify gate is the conversational-to-deterministic boundary: only on ratification
  does atdd plan (the system, not the agent) invoke atdd author <kind> per locked
  unit.'

statement: 'An atdd plan decomposition needs no PRE-EXISTING issue or up-front ceremony,
  but it MUST be bound to a local ATDD issue record before Ratify: on Ratify, atdd plan
  binds the locked decomposition to a target issue (or mints one from the main job) and
  authors the plan as that issue''s PLANNED-phase substrate on its registered branch +
  worktree. The binding identity is the LOCAL manifest/State Store record (its slug; #945/#1168),
  not a GitHub issue number — GitHub is a downstream extension that syncs the number after
  install, so the iron rule (issue + branch + worktree per repo modification) holds even
  with no GitHub. The session removes the up-front ceremony, not the i

statement: Ratify cannot lock a user/system-flow-bearing plan when required flow router sanity
  fails.

statement: Ratify names the rungs of the granularity ladder a decomposition did not
  descend, so an operator is told that a locked plan is not testable end to end rather
  than having to notice it.

statement: 'atdd plan runs a gated decomposition session: Intent -> Attach -> Compose
  -> Ratify, then author -> verify -> modify. The stages name what the OPERATOR is
  deciding, not what the tool is doing. Stages are gates not scripts (free dialogue
  within a stage; backtracking allowed); a stage advances only when its exit condition
  (proper state) holds. These are the SESSION stages, and they are a separate
  vocabulary from the DESIRED OUTCOME job steps owned by steps.convention — do not read the two
  as one system.'

statement: A hand-authored plan unit spec is validated against its artifact schema
  — well-formedness at Compose, completeness at Ratify — so the by-construction guarantee
  atdd author makes is kept at the one layer where the spec is written by hand.

statement: Every convention node (any *.convention.yaml carrying a rule_id, test fixtures excluded) must appear as a source_ref or target_ref of at least one edge in the relationship graph (src/atdd/coach/graph/relationships.yaml). A node referenced by no edge is an orphan and is refused — the graph must cover every node, not just have no dangling edges.

statement: 'A feature marked `kind: feedback-loop` must have at least one SMOKE acceptance
  whose acceptance block declares a close_the_loop: field carrying both consumer_reacted
  and drift_resolved.'

statement: Each JTBD step declares its primary architecture layer(s) and a canonical
  call sequence across presentation, application, domain, and integration, giving
  a routable mapping from step to architecture.

statement: Every job decomposes into an ordered sequence of nine JTBD steps — define,
  locate, prepare, confirm, execute, monitor, modify, resolve, conclude — each with
  a fixed purpose, guiding question, and expected outputs.

statement: Each JTBD step is recognized and phrased through a fixed set of slotted
  linguistic templates that bind the step's verb to its objects and constraints.

statement: Steps are ordered and numbered, and each declares its pre-conditions and
  its outputs.

statement: A subject is a durable noun object registered in plan/_subjects.yaml before
  any user/system flow is typed under it; subjects are unique-by-subject and typed user/system flows are
  unique-by-subject+slug.

statement: >-
  Every acceptance declares telemetry with disposition required (naming at least one concrete
  telemetry URN that resolves to a tracking-plan entry) or disposition not-applicable (with a
  rationale), and every tracking-plan item's acceptance references resolve to declared acceptances
  (REQUIRED).

statement: >-
  Every concrete tracking-plan item's logical artifact is produced by exactly one product capability's
  produce[] telemetry declaration, and the item's owner names that product capability (REQUIRED).

statement: >-
  Metric tracking-plan items declare only low- or medium-cardinality dimensions, and no dimension
  names a property declared cardinality high (REQUIRED).

statement: >-
  Every JSON file under the telemetry root is one concrete tracking-plan item at
  `telemetry/<theme>/<artifact>/{event|trace|metric|log}.<plane>[.<measure>].json`, shape-valid
  against telemetry-plan.schema.json, with its id and logical artifact mirroring its path, a SemVer
  version, and no concrete id declared twice (REQUIRED).

statement: A theme is a repository-defined kebab-case namespace for plan artifacts. The only
  reserved entry is index 0, which MUST be commons; repositories declare every other theme
  in plan/_themes.yaml. Theme membership and identity-prefix consistency are enforceable.

statement: Every product capability, user/system flow, flow router, and contract theme MUST resolve to a value in the
  repository-owned plan/_themes.yaml registry. The package provides no default taxonomy.

statement: 'plan/_themes.yaml MUST declare commons at theme index 0. Repositories may add any
  valid theme at other indexes, but may not replace or remove the commons floor.'

statement: A themed product capability's produced artifact, contract, and telemetry identity prefix MUST equal
  the product capability theme.

statement: Every platform:acceptance:commit-failure.cause (version_conflict, authorization_refused, idempotency_conflict, authority_unavailable) MUST be reachable, registered in the dispatch graph, resolvable, and terminating - or an explicit tracked-and-expiring deferral. Pending binding - validator owned by D5 (#1089).

statement: A user/system flow may carry an optional acceptances block (DESIRED OUTCOME acceptance shape);
  each contributes a derived repo rule via the rule-binding walker.

statement: Artifacts flow between participants as {domain}:{resource}; they must be produced before consumed
  and be defined in participant product capability manifests.

statement: "The category FIELD classifies a user/system flow as nominal, error, alternate, or exception. It is
  metadata on the user/system flow, never encoded in its identity, so reclassifying a user/system flow
  changes a field and not its name."

statement: A user/system flow is an executable end-to-end system/user journey — a strictly-linear,
  ordered sequence of steps that moves artifacts across a set of product capabilities from a declared
  initial input to exactly one terminal contract, telling ONE coherent journey. This
  is a planner domain-decomposition artifact naming WHAT journey the domain must support;
  how the journey is run and whether it holds state at runtime are coder/tester concerns.
  This node is an advisory semantic anchor — it enforces nothing directly; the enforceable
  parts of this meaning are decomposed into the constraint/rule nodes that require it.

statement: A user/system flow references prerequisite user/system flows as user-system-flow:{user_system_flow_id}; foundation (commons) user/system flows often
  precede others; data-flow consumers depend on producers; circular dependencies are forbidden.

statement: 'A composite (artifact_urn, discriminant) -> user_system_flow_id dispatch key is exceptional:
  permitted only with a behavioral_difference justification, discriminant exactly
  one field:value.'

statement: The divergence dispatch map is a declared, schema-valid registry (artifact_urn
  -> user_system_flow_id) that the journey router reads; routing is never an imperative in-code
  map.

statement: The declared family MUST agree with the declared terminal contract - family:delivery iff the terminal requires an Acceptance Authority commit AND the terminal primary is platform:acceptance:commit-receipt; family:behavior otherwise; a missing family field is invalid. Pending binding - validator owned by D1 (#1085).

statement: The family classifies a user/system flow as behavior or delivery, orthogonal to the variant category (0-3). The declared terminal contract is the source of truth; the family field is the validator-checked assertion and is never encoded in the user/system flow ID.

statement: Every DESIRED OUTCOME obligation surfaces as message, self-message, guard, fragment,
  invariant, or explicit structural residual.

statement: Flow routers select routes and declare payload contract identities; they
  must not contain flow-variable runtime values or artifact data.

statement: Every flow router declares whether it is runtime-exposed and which Station
  Master actions are expected to reach it.

statement: Every guarded alt/opt fragment binds to acceptance(s), and flow-branch
  acceptances bind back to guards/fragments.

statement: Every executable guard path in a flow router maps to exactly one user/system flow
  route, unless explicitly classified as structural residual.

statement: Flow router guards are declarative, deterministic, side-effect-free expressions;
  raw Python eval is forbidden.

statement: Flow router artifacts live under plan/_user_system_flows/_flow_routers/ and are
  registered in plan/_user_system_flows/_flow_routers.yaml.

statement: Every flow router message declares a payload contract or an explicit no-payload
  reason.

statement: A payload contract identity referenced by a flow router message must
  resolve to a contract schema body.

statement: A payload contract identity referenced by a flow router message must
  resolve to an authored/registered contract in the contracts registry, not merely
  a file that glob-matches.

statement: A referenced user/system flow sequence must equal the flow router route projection
  by step, intent, from, to, and artifact.

statement: Every flow router route declares nominal/error/alternate/exception and
  that category must equal the `category` field of the target user/system flow it selects
  (issue #1421 — category is a validated field, not an identity digit).

statement: Route resolution strategy is explicit and deterministic; ambiguous matching
  routes fail closed unless unique priority is declared.

statement: Structural residuals must be explicit, narrow, and bound to an acceptance
  and validator.

statement: A user/system flow MUST declare every artifact flow variables may be seeded with - inputs.caller (caller-provided) and inputs.spec_materialized (deterministically materialized from the spec). Undeclared or missing required initial inputs are rejected before step 1. Pending binding - validator owned by D2 (#1086).

statement: 'User/system flows are strictly linear: sequences contain steps only — no loops, routes, or branching;
  new paths MUST become new user/system flows.'

statement: user_system_flow_id is the typed identity user-system-flow:{subject}:{descriptive-name}, with
  kebab-case subject and descriptive name; title is Title Case; files are flat at
  plan/_user_system_flows/{user_system_flow_id}.yaml.

statement: 'Participants are the actors in a user/system flow workflow: capability:{id}, user:{role}, or system:{source};
  each listed once.'

statement: User/system flows are production orchestration (not test infrastructure), executed by FlowRunner under
  python/user-system-flows/.

statement: Every row in plan/_user_system_flows.yaml must name a path that is a file on disk, and
  every per-user/system-flow document under plan/_user_system_flows must be named by a registry row. Coherence
  is bidirectional - a row naming an absent document is a dangling pointer consumers
  resolve through, and a document no row names is an orphan.

statement: 'Each user/system flow needs two files: a registry entry in plan/_user_system_flows.yaml and a full spec at plan/_user_system_flows/{user_system_flow_id}.yaml;
  every registry entry MUST have a corresponding spec file.'

statement: 'Every flow router must assess each route category: nominal requires one
  or more routes, and alternate/error/exception each require routes or a typed not-applicable
  basis from a closed vocabulary (issue #1554).'

statement: 'Every registered user/system flow must be targeted by exactly one registered flow router
  route, or declare a typed single-route assessment; absence of a route no longer
  implies direct dispatch (issue #1554).'

statement: 'A user/system flow tells ONE coherent journey: 3-7 product capabilities (sweet spot), 2 minimum, 8-12 review, 13+ decompose;
  if you can''t state the outcome in one sentence without ''and'', split it.'

statement: A sequence is ordered workflow steps; each step transfers one artifact (step, intent, from,
  to, artifact). (Loop/route elements are documented but forbidden under the linearity rule.)

statement: A user/system flow's terminal step declares exactly one primary artifact. That terminal contract is the source of truth for the user/system flow's family - if it requires an Acceptance Authority commit and terminates in platform:acceptance:commit-receipt the user/system flow is delivery, otherwise it is behavior.

statement: A user/system flow declares its themes explicitly; most product capabilities should match the primary declared theme; secondary
  themes are allowed when a user/system flow spans multiple themes.

statement: Theme orchestrator files (python/user-system-flows/orchestrators/{theme}.py) carry user-system-flow:{theme}:{user_system_flow_id}
  URN lines, one per implemented user/system flow.
statement: Each user/system flow declares one or more named themes. Themes classify the journey; they are not encoded in the user/system flow identity.

statement: A user/system flow must satisfy the documented validation rules (typed id, declared themes, spec file
  exists, participants declared, valid dependencies, domain:resource artifacts, category declared as a
  field).
statement: Create user/system flow variations within a theme by mode, complexity, persona, or phase.

statement: >-
  Before a delivery that Flow tracks with an owner-inspection/v1 record is accepted, the record Flow already read
  MUST be acceptable evidence for the exact candidate: published for that commit, its tracked evidence digests
  still matching, aimed only at a loopback local target, built on synthetic data, carrying teardown evidence,
  stating N/A only for a toolkit surface with a rationale and one of the direct evidence kinds Flow defines for
  N/A, and acknowledged by operator@desk before done. Flow alone owns the record shape, publication, acknowledgement and
  cleanup lifecycle; ATDD Bun only reports findings and never writes, publishes, stores, or copies any of it.

statement: >-
  Before a delivery may be accepted after its deterministic CI and convention gates pass, a final reviewer
  MUST reconcile the observable behavior of the assembled system with the declared intent that motivated the
  work. Passing tests, a clean diff, and green convention checks are supporting evidence; none is a substitute
  for observing that the delivered behavior matches the plan. The review MUST establish expected behavior
  from the relevant acceptance, product capability, user/system flow, flow router, journey, and delivery criteria before relying on
  implementation details; exercise the highest meaningful assembled boundary; compare the observed result
  with that int

statement: >-
  The agent proposes profiles without being asked: when the work reaches a stage whose preset is not active yet (RED starts while only planner is on, or no profiles: list is set), it asks the user what they want to do and recommends the matching preset. It explains that presets are adopted gradually, each the set most consistent with that work, so nothing needs activating all at once. The user decides; the agent writes only what they choose. Presets accumulate: moving on adds profiles, it never swaps them, because removing one loosens the gate.

statement: A feature that owns DESIRED OUTCOMES has at least one source component beneath `<source_root>/<capability>/features/<feature>/`.
  Package rule, strict.

statement: Every product capability is declared at `<plan_root>/<capability>/_<capability>.yaml`, every feature at `<plan_root>/<capability>/<feature>.yaml`,
  and every DESIRED OUTCOME at `<plan_root>/<capability>/<DESIRED_OUTCOME>.yaml`. Package rule, strict.

statement: 'When the plan models at least one product capability, feature or DESIRED OUTCOME, every source file beneath `<source_root>`
  carries `URN: component:{capability}:{feature}:{name}:{frontend|backend}:{domain|application|integration|presentation}`
  and lives beneath `<source_root>/<capability>/features/<feature>/`, for a feature the plan declares. Package rule,
  strict.'
statement: Each identified implementation component declares a testing witness.
statement: Each implementation testing witness resolves to an identified Bun test.

statement: 'A spec identified as accessibility (an `A11Y` test URN, or an `a11y` token in its file name) MUST import
  `AxeBuilder` from `@axe-core/playwright` (under any local name), call `new AxeBuilder(...).analyze()`, and assert
  on the returned `violations` in a way that can fail: equal to none (`toEqual([])`, `toHaveLength(0)`, `toBe(0)`)
  or bounded (`toBeLessThanOrEqual(n)`, `toBeLessThan(n)`). A tautology such as `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0)` is not
  an assertion. Bun/htmx realization of `tester.vite.a11y-harness`, strict.'

statement: >-
  A test file carrying a URN MUST also declare `// Acceptance: acc:…` or, for a journey/E2E test, `//
  UserSystemFlow: …`. Stack-neutral obligation, Bun-specific detector. Realized by
  `bun_tester_discipline_detector`.

statement: >-
  A `// @covers` tag above an `it()` MUST name a well-formed `acc:{capability}:{ACCEPTANCE-ID}` URN. Stack-
  neutral obligation, Bun-specific detector implementing the two-level binding model. Realized by
  `bun_tester_discipline_detector`.

statement: >-
  A test's `// Acceptance:` and `// DESIRED_OUTCOME:` headers MUST name artifacts the plan actually declares.
  Declaring a binding is not the same as having one: a suite bound to an acceptance that exists
  nowhere is attributed to nothing, and every coverage figure computed from it is fiction. Core owns
  the shape of these artifacts; only a per-stack detector can see whether a Bun test resolves into
  them.

statement: When the repository declares a plan, the user/system flow or journey a journey spec binds to MUST be declared under
  `plan/`. Bun/htmx realization of `tester.vite.e2e-names-valid-user-system-flow`, strict.

statement: A declared user/system flow that a journey spec binds to MUST be selected by at least one flow router route. Bun/htmx
  realization of `tester.vite.covered-user-system-flow-is-routed`, strict.

statement: Every journey whose entrypoint is exposed and whose `surfaces` include `frontend` (or declare none) MUST
  have at least one journey spec bound to it by `// Journey:` with an E2E or SMOKE test URN. New in the Bun/htmx
  browser tester, strict.

statement: A file that imports `@playwright/test` and declares tests (`test(...)`, `test.describe(...)`) MUST be
  named `*.e2e.ts` (`.js`, `.mjs`, `.tsx` variants allowed). `bun test` collects every `*.test.*` and `*.spec.*`
  file, so a Playwright spec named that way is executed by the wrong runner and fails, or worse is skipped by a
  filter nobody remembers. New in the Bun/htmx browser tester, strict.

statement: Every human-facing user/system flow declared under `plan/` (one in which a `user:` participant takes part) MUST
  have at least one journey spec bound to it by `// UserSystemFlow:`. Bun/htmx realization of `tester.vite.user-system-flow-e2e-coverage`,
  strict.

statement: >-
  A test that exercises a flow router MUST drive the production runtime objects — `FlowRouterRunner`
  (route resolution) and `FlowRunner` (linear user/system flow execution), the core afokapu/atdd#1251 call model —
  and MUST NOT substitute a mock, a substituted runner, or a
  hand-built route resolver for them. This is the Bun-stack realization of the agnostic core
  obligation `tester.flow-router.production-runner-used`; its JS detector (a member of the
  `bun_flow_router_coverage` FAMILY) scans the consumer's `e2e/**/*.ts` flow router tests and flags
  any that fail to reference both production runner symbols or that carry a forbidden substitution
  pattern. A flow router t

statement: >-
  Every admissible route declared in a flow router's guarded route space (the `routes:` list of
  `plan/_user_system_flows/_flow_routers/**/*.yaml`, the authoritative route space locked by core
  afokapu/atdd#1248) MUST have at least one end-to-end test that exercises it — an `e2e/**/*.ts` test
  that names the route by its `routeId` or its resolved `userSystemFlowId` so its resolution is proven through
  the production FlowRouterRunner -> FlowRunner path (core afokapu/atdd#1251), not asserted
  descriptively. This is the Bun-stack realization of the agnostic core obligation
  `tester.flow-router.route-coverage`; its JS detector (a member of the `bun_flow_router_coverage`
  FAM

statement: >-
  Every exposed journey router action of a flow router (`entrypoint.exposed: true` with an `actions:`
  entry, core afokapu/atdd#1248) MUST have a smoke test that drives the action through the real
  entrypoint -> journey router -> FlowRouterRunner -> FlowRunner path (core afokapu/atdd#1251). This
  is the Bun-stack realization of the agnostic core obligation
  `tester.flow-router.smoke-coverage-for-journey-router`; its JS detector (a member of the
  `bun_flow_router_coverage` FAMILY) scans the flow router entrypoints and the consumer's
  `e2e/**/*.ts` tests and flags any exposed action with no smoke test that reaches the journey router and
  exercises the production runners. E

statement: >-
  A test that asserts on the runtime trace emitted by flow router execution MUST bind that trace back to
  the source flow router declaration — it must assert every required trace field so the executed route is
  traceable to the flow router YAML it came from (core afokapu/atdd#1248 route space, #1251 runtime
  trace). This is the Bun-stack realization of the agnostic core obligation
  `tester.flow-router.trace-binds-declared-route`; its JS detector (a member of the
  `bun_flow_router_coverage` FAMILY) scans the consumer's `e2e/**/*.ts` flow router trace tests and
  flags any that reference the runtime `trace` but omit one or more required binding fields. A trace
  assertion th

statement: >-
  Every user/system flow reachable from a declared flow router route MUST have a test that asserts the product capability
  SEQUENCE it executes — the ordered steps, not merely which user/system flow was selected. Route resolution
  and trace binding both prove WHICH user/system flow was chosen; neither proves WHAT it ran. Without this a
  user/system flow definition can be reordered, shortened or emptied and the suite stays green.

statement: >-
  A test case that performs an HTTP request and asserts on the response status MUST also assert on the
  response BODY. Bun/htmx-specific obligation with no counterpart in any other stack's tester extension.
  Realized by `bun_tester_discipline_detector`.

statement: >-
  A test case that asserts an out-of-band swap is present in a response MUST also assert the destination
  `id`. Bun/htmx realization: the tester half of `coder.htmx.swap-oob-carries-id`, and the same shape as
  `tester.convex.flow-router-trace-binds-declared-route` — an assertion on a runtime artefact must bind
  back to the declaration it came from.

statement: >-
  Every endpoint declared by an htmx verb attribute (`hx-get`, `hx-post`, `hx-put`, `hx-patch`, `hx-
  delete`) MUST be exercised by at least one test. Bun/htmx realization mirroring
  `tester.convex.flow-router-route-coverage`; the declaration source differs, and that difference IS the
  adaptation — a Convex route is declared in `plan/_user_system_flows/_flow_routers/**/*.yaml`, an htmx endpoint is
  declared in the MARKUP, so the markup is this stack's route space.

statement: 'A journey spec (a `*.e2e.ts` file, or any test file whose header comments carry a `// UserSystemFlow:`, `// Journey:`
  or `// URN: test:userSystemFlow|journey:` marker) MUST carry exactly one binding header: `// UserSystemFlow: user-system-flow:<subject>:<slug>`
  or `// Journey: journey:<id>`, each matching the planner''s identity grammar. Bun/htmx realization of `tester.vite.journey-user-system-flow-header`,
  strict.'

statement: 'A journey spec MUST carry `// Layer: assembly`. Bun/htmx realization of `tester.vite.journey-layer-assembly`,
  strict.'

statement: A journey spec, meaning a browser spec (a `*.e2e.*` file, or a Playwright file bound to a user/system flow or journey), MUST NOT carry `// Acceptance:` or `// DESIRED_OUTCOME:` header lines; a bun test file is never a journey spec. Bun/htmx realization of `tester.vite.journey-no-acceptance-marker`,
  strict.

statement: A journey spec MUST carry at least one test URN `test:{userSystemFlow|journey}:<id>:{E2E|SMOKE|A11Y|VIS|RESP}-NNN-<slug>`,
  and every URN it carries MUST be well-formed and name the subject its binding header declares. Bun/htmx realization
  of `tester.vite.journey-urn-format`, strict.

statement: >-
  A test whose Phase is RED MUST assert behaviour; a case whose assertions are all existence checks
  (`toBeDefined` / `toBeTruthy` / `toBeFalsy` / `toBeNull` / `toBeUndefined`), or which asserts nothing at
  all, is refused. Stack-neutral obligation, Bun-specific detector over `bun:test` matchers. Realized by
  `bun_tester_discipline_detector`.

statement: >-
  A test whose Phase is RED MUST contain at least one guaranteed-fail marker. Accepted markers,
  transcribed from CORE `red.convention.yaml` -> `red_patterns.typescript`: `throw new Error('Not
  implemented …')`, `throw new UnimplementedError(…)`, `expect(false).toBe(true)`,
  `expect(true).toBe(false)`, `expect.fail(…)`, `return Promise.reject(…)`, and `it.fails(` /
  `test.failing(`. Bun realization of core `tester.red.test-must-fail-first`, mirroring
  `tester.convex.red-fails-first` rule for rule.

statement: 'A spec identified as responsive (a `RESP` test URN, or a `responsive`/`resp` token in its file name)
  MUST render the page at every viewport width declared in `atdd-bun.yaml` under `frontend.viewports` (default 375,
  768, 1280), through `page.setViewportSize({ width })`, a `viewport: { width }` option, or a list of widths it
  iterates (`for (const w of [...])`, `LIST.forEach`, `LIST.map`); picking one element of a list renders one width.
  It MUST pass `scrollWidth`, directly or through a variable measured from it, to an `expect(...)` so the test fails
  when the page overflows horizontally. New in the Bun/htmx browser tester, strict.'

statement: Every journey whose entrypoint is exposed and whose `surfaces` include `frontend` (or declare none) MUST
  have a journey spec bound to it by `// Journey:` with a RESP test URN. New in the Bun/htmx browser tester, strict.

statement: >-
  A test file that declares a `// Runtime:` MUST name a runtime in the JS/TS family (`bun`, `browser`,
  `isomorphic`, `typescript`, `ts`, `node`, `js`, `javascript`, `deno`, `vite`, `astro`, `preact`). Bun
  realization mirroring `tester.convex.routing-path`, which makes the same argument for Vitest.

statement: >-
  A test identified as a security test by its URN kind segment (`-SEC-`, `-RLS-`, `-AUTH-`) MUST contain
  an authentication/authorisation assertion — an expectation tied to 401, 403, unauthorised, forbidden,
  denied, permission, `.rejects` or `toThrow`. Bun realization of core `tester.security.auth`, mirroring
  `tester.convex.security-auth`.

statement: >-
  A test identified as an input-validation test by its URN kind segment (`-INPUT-`, `-VALIDATION-`,
  `-VALIDATE-`) MUST contain a rejection assertion — `.rejects`, `toThrow`, 400, 422, invalid, reject, or
  an error expectation. Bun realization of core `tester.security.input`, mirroring
  `tester.convex.security-input`.

statement: >-
  A test whose Phase is SMOKE MUST NOT substitute a production collaborator — `mock.module`, `spyOn`,
  `jest.mock`/`spyOn`, `vi.mock`/`spyOn`. Stack-neutral obligation, Bun-specific substitution vocabulary
  (`bun:test` exposes `mock` and `spyOn` where pytest uses `monkeypatch`). Realized by
  `bun_tester_discipline_detector`.

statement: >-
  A test whose Phase is SMOKE MUST assert on an operator-observable channel — HTTP response status or
  body, rendered markup, stdout/stderr, exit code — and not only on objects the test constructed itself.
  Stack-neutral obligation, Bun/htmx-specific channel vocabulary. Realized by
  `bun_tester_discipline_detector`.

statement: Every `.tsx`/`.jsx` component under a `presentation/` path segment MUST be covered by a SMOKE browser
  spec whose path names the component's product capability (the segment before `presentation`). Bun/htmx realization of `tester.vite.presentation-smoke-coverage`,
  strict.

statement: >-
  A telemetry test contains an assertion on the emission itself — `toHaveBeenCalled[With|Times]`, or
  an expectation on `.emit` / `.emitted` / `.capture` / `.track` / `.record` (REQUIRED).

statement: >-
  A test identified as a telemetry test by its URN kind segment (`-TELEMETRY-`, `-EVENT-`, `-METRIC-`) or
  by `*.telemetry.test.*` colocation MUST contain an emission assertion — `toHaveBeenCalled[With|Times]`,
  or an expectation on `.emit` / `.emitted` / `.capture` / `.track` / `.record`. Bun realization of core
  `tester.telemetry.emit`, mirroring `tester.convex.telemetry-emit`.

statement: >-
  Every concrete telemetry URN a telemetry test claims in its `// Telemetry:` header appears in
  the test's code as an assertion string; a telemetry test with no header asserts at least one
  concrete telemetry URN (REQUIRED).

statement: >-
  Every concrete telemetry item an acceptance requires is bound by at least one test file's
  `// Telemetry:` header (REQUIRED).

statement: >-
  A `// Telemetry:` reference in a test file is well-formed, resolves to a tracking-plan item, and
  the test carries an `Acceptance:` binding to a declared acceptance whose telemetry decision
  requires that item (REQUIRED).

statement: >-
  Every timing semantic a tracking-plan item declares (post-commit, absent-after-rollback,
  correlation-across-async) is exercised by at least one telemetry test bound to that item
  (REQUIRED).

statement: >-
  Every `*.test.*` / `*.spec.*` file MUST carry a `// URN: test:{capability}:{feature}:{ACCEPTANCE-ID}` header.
  Stack-neutral obligation, Bun-specific line-comment detector. Core's counterpart is explicit that a
  test's authoritative identity is its HEADER and not its filename, and this realization follows that
  exactly — it never parses a filename for identity. Realized by `bun_tester_discipline_detector`.

statement: >-
  A test file in a Bun stack MUST import its harness from `bun:test` and MUST NOT import `vitest`,
  `jest`, `@jest/globals`, `mocha` or `chai`. The workspace provider's declared runner is `bun`, so a
  test bound to a foreign harness is not executed by the runner the gate believes it ran. This is the
  Bun-stack realization of the agnostic "the declared runner is the runner that runs" obligation,
  enforced by the `bun_fullstack_detector` family implementation on `atdd.workspace.bun`.

statement: >-
  A test MUST NOT mutate `process.env` nor write to a filesystem path outside a temp directory. Stack-
  neutral obligation, RE-REALIZED for this stack: core's sibling detects Python bare-mode-init patterns,
  which do not exist here. Realized by `bun_tester_discipline_detector`.

statement: >-
  A test MUST NOT disable itself with `.skip` / `.todo` / `.failing`, nor bail out early on an environment
  check. Stack-neutral obligation, Bun-specific detector over `bun:test` modifiers. Realized by
  `bun_tester_discipline_detector`.

statement: >-
  A test file carrying a URN MUST declare `// Phase:` with one of RED, UNIT, SMOKE, E2E. Stack-neutral
  obligation, Bun-specific detector. Realized by `bun_tester_discipline_detector`.

statement: 'Every flow router route has `<e2e_root>/flow-routers/<flow-router>/<route>.routes.test.ts`, and every
  exposed journey `<e2e_root>/journeys/<journey>.journey.test.ts`, each carrying a `test:{capability}:{feature}:{acceptance}`
  URN for a declared feature and binding `Acceptance: acc:{capability}:{acceptance}` declared by a DESIRED OUTCOME. On an exposed
  journey whose surfaces include `frontend`, a Playwright spec (`*.e2e.ts`) substitutes for the Bun test when it
  is bound to the route''s user/system flow (`// UserSystemFlow:`) or the journey (`// Journey:`) and carries a valid E2E or SMOKE test
  URN for that same subject (`test:user-system-flow:<id>:E2E-NNN-…`, `test:journe
statement: A feature that owns DESIRED OUTCOMES has at least one test bound to one of its acceptances. Package rule, strict.

statement: 'When the plan models at least one product capability, feature or DESIRED OUTCOME, every test beneath `<test_root>` carries `URN:
  test:{capability}:{feature}:{acceptance}`, lives beneath `<test_root>/<capability>/features/<feature>/{unit,contract,integration}/`,
  and binds `Acceptance: acc:{capability}:{acceptance}` declared by a DESIRED OUTCOME that the test''s own feature lists. Package
  rule, strict.'
statement: Every declared acceptance is bound by at least one Bun test.
statement: Each identified Bun test names a plan acceptance, DESIRED OUTCOME, or user/system flow that resolves.

statement: A spec identified as visual (a `VIS` test URN, or a `visual`/`vis` token in its file name) MUST call
  `toHaveScreenshot()` or `toMatchSnapshot()`. Bun/htmx realization of `tester.vite.visual-harness`, strict.

statement: >-
  Agents use accountable delegation, evidence-based escalation, economical delivery,
  and bounded two-way resolution while keeping work within its assigned project and task.

statement: >-
  When the workflow profile is active, agents coordinate durable work through the locally installed
  atdd-flow CLI and its YAML coordination root. A seat owns its runtime binding, branch and
  worktree; a task owns its delivery state and proof; a thread owns its conversation. Drivers favor
  the smallest effective implementation, coordinate shared-boundary decisions through their
  coordinators, and continue assigned work until it is review-ready or explicitly blocked.
